transcript.text:
I can help you work through this. "Not working properly" can mean a few different things on a hob, so I need to check the simple settings first before looking at faults. 1. 2. If it's an induction hob, the pan you're using might not be magnetic or suitable.
3. A genuine fault with that specific heating element, switch, or internal board. 1. Look for a key or padlock symbol on the control panel. If you see one, hold it down for 3-5 seconds to unlock the hob. Then try turning a zone on again.
2. Identify your hob type: is it induction (digital touch controls, glass only) or ceramic/radiant (glowing red rings or solid metal plates)? Let me know if the lock was on and what type of hob you have.
It's a ceramic one with the touch controls, a Zanussi. I don't think the lock is on, no padlock showing. Only the rear right ring isn't working, the others are fine.

Since the other zones work fine, we can rule out a general power supply issue or a main board failure affecting everything. On a ceramic hob with touch controls, when one specific zone stops heating while the others work, it is almost always either the heating element for that zone itself (the coil underneath has burnt out) or the energy regulator (simmerstat) that controls the power to that zone. 1. If you can safely do so with the hob switched off and unplugged, check if the rear right ring is a solid metal plate or if you can see a coil structure under the glass. 2. If it's a solid plate (or if you're unsure but want to test), turn that specific zone on for about 5 minutes. Watch closely: does it get hot at all, or does it stay completely cold? Does it get warm but never reach cooking temperature? Please let me know what happens when you try that.

I tried it and the rear right ring doesn't glow red at all and no heat. The number does show on the display though. It's a ceramic glass top so I can't see any coil underneath, and I'm not taking it apart.

Since that specific zone shows a number on the display but produces absolutely no heat or glow, and the other zones are working fine, this suggests the control logic is functioning. The issue is isolated to the power delivery or the heating component for that rear right ring. The most likely cause is that the radiant heating element underneath the glass has burnt out. On ceramic hobs with solid plates or hidden coils, once an element fails, it simply won't heat up again. A less common possibility is a fault in the energy regulator (simmerstat) or the wiring connecting to that zone. Because you are not taking the hob apart, there is no further owner-safe check we can do to distinguish between a failed element and a failed regulator/switch. Both components are located under the glass top and require dismantling to access and test with a multimeter. Given this is likely an internal component failure (element or regulator), you will need to call in a qualified engineer to replace the faulty part. If the hob is still within its warranty period, contact Zanussi support first; otherwise, a local appliance repair technician can usually replace these parts relatively quickly.

Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
